newsitem.title: USA: Boskin CPI recommendations to include legislation.
newsitem.headline: Boskin CPI recommendations to include legislation.

text.p: Stanford University professor Michael Boskin said Wednesday his commission will have recommendations for the president, Congress and the Bureau of Labor Statistics, including legislation, in its long-awaited Consumer Price Index report.
He declined to say specifically what the recommendations would be and would also not confirm reports that the panel will declare that the CPI has an upward bias of 1.1 percent.
Boskin spoke with reporters prior to giving remarks to a conference sponsored by the American Enterprise Institute.

"The only thing I'm prepared to say now is that there will be two classes of recommendations, more than a dozen to the BLS on ways they can accelerate their programs to improve the nation's price statistics, on which they are already making some progress," he said.
In addition, he said, "The second set will be a set of recommendations to the president and the Congress on things they should be doing in light of these results."

He said also that the body of the report will contain a recommendation on the bias of the CPI as well as a very substantial explanation and documentation "on how we came to the conclusions that we did."

Asked if the report would contain recommendations for legislation, Boskin declined to be specific but said, "There are some recommendations for legislation but I'm not prepared to discuss them at this time."
The commission, which was named by Congress a year and a half ago to study the CPI, will release its official report at 12:30 p.m. (1730 GMT).
